messages:
olivia: Quick Q — we're planning to migrate service `proxy-gateway` from an NLB (tcp passthrough) to an ALB (https) so we can offload TLS with ACM. Two quick concerns: a) will backend pods see real client IPs? b) what's the minimal terraform/ingress change (we use aws-lb-controller + ALB ingress) to wire certs from ACM or cert-manager? Any gotchas re health checks / target group behavior?

rahul: Short answers: ALB is L7 so backend pods won't see the raw client source IP at the network level. ALB adds X-Forwarded-For header which most apps can consume. If you absolutely need the original TCP source IP you either need NLB (proxy protocol) or a passthrough setup (no TLS termination at ALB). ALB does NOT support proxy protocol for HTTP listeners.

jordan: Also note `service.spec.externalTrafficPolicy=Local` only helps for NLB/nodePort flow to preserve node source IP; it won't make the pod see the client IP when ALB terminates TLS. For ALB, rely on X-Forwarded-For or have your app read `X-Forwarded-For` header.

maria: For certs, with AWS Load Balancer Controller the usual pattern is to reference an ACM cert via annotations on the Ingress, e.g.:

```
metadata:
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:123456789012:certificate/abcd-efgh
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTP":80},{"HTTPS":443}]'
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internet-facing
```

If you want cert-manager to manage certificates inside the cluster you would instead terminate in-cluster (NGINX/Contour) and use cert-manager to populate a `tls` secret. Pick one termination model and stick with it for a single service. Mixing causes confusion.

olivia: From a terraform perspective — do we need to replace the aws_lb resources or will the aws-lb-controller CRD create the ALB for us? We currently manage the NLB via terraform.

rahul: If you let the AWS LB Controller create the ALB (via the Ingress CRD) you won't need terraform for the ALB. If you manage it in terraform you will create `aws_lb`, `aws_lb_listener` and `aws_lb_target_group` etc. Most teams either: 1) manage the ALB in k8s (recommended for app-driven routing) or 2) manage the ALB in terraform and point it at k8s targets. The middle ground is painful.

sophie: Practical TF diffs to watch for if you move from NLB->ALB and manage in TF: target type should be `ip` for pod-backed target groups, listener protocol will be `HTTPS`, and you'll attach `certificate_arn` on the listener. Also update the LB SG to allow 443 from internet and ensure nodes' SG allows inbound from ALB SG on nodePort range.

rahul: Example TF resources you might add/remove: `aws_lb` (ALB), `aws_lb_listener` (443 with cert), `aws_lb_target_group` (target_type = "ip"), and remove `aws_lb_target_group_attachment` if using ip targets (k8s controller handles attachments). Don't forget IAM policy changes for the controller (it needs permissions to manage ALBs).

olivia: Health checks — any special config? Our app uses TLS on 8443 currently when fronted by NLB.

sophie: If ALB terminates TLS, health checks must be HTTP(S) and hit an HTTP path (e.g. `/healthz`). Make the target group health check port match the pod port (or use traffic port) and set `healthy_threshold`/`interval` low enough for faster failover. If you still want TLS to pod, use TCP NLB.

jordan: Another gotcha: sticky sessions/cookie-based affinity changes. ALB supports ALB cookie stickiness; if your app relied on source-IP stickiness from NLB that will change. Also path-based routing rules on ALB may require more granular Ingress rules.

maria: Secrets wiring note: If terminating in ALB with ACM, you don't need a k8s `tls` secret. If terminating in-cluster, cert-manager creates a `kubernetes.io/tls` secret in the service namespace and your Ingress references it under `spec.tls`. Don't forget RBAC and issuer config for cert-manager.

olivia: thanks. Plan: do a staging canary — create a new namespace `proxy-canary` with `ingressClass=alb`, let the k8s ingress CRD create the ALB (so TF changes minimal), test traffic, validate X-Forwarded-For behavior and health checks. Will open a TF/infra PR for the SG and RBAC bits. :eyes:

rahul: lgtm — ping me when the PR is up, I can review the controller/IAM bits. :thumbsup:

sophie: reminder — security group change required: allow ALB-SG -> node-SG on nodePort range (30000-32767) or the pod port if using hostNetwork.

olivia: noted, will add SG rules in the PR. I'll also add a short test harness to assert `X-Forwarded-For` present in app logs and check health endpoint responses.

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for infra/staging — 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. Details: will add security group rule from ALB SG -> node SG.

jordan: small ops note — if the ALB is internet-facing, make sure certificate's domain covers the test host and ACM cert is in the same region as the ALB.

olivia: will do. Thanks all, will circle back with the PR link later.
